battle.name: 英國入侵拉普拉塔河
battle.theater: 拉普拉塔河口布宜諾斯艾利斯
battle.brief: 一八〇六年英國遠征船隊駛入拉普拉塔河，兵鋒直指布宜諾斯艾利斯；翌年再以逾萬兵力攻城，兩度兵臨城下，終因攻城受挫與歐洲局勢逆轉而撤回。卡面的燧發槍是英軍線性齊射的骨幹，也是守軍手中同型的舊式步槍。

kit.name: 燧發槍
kit.history: 擊錘打火比火繩穩。線性列陣的射速和精度都靠它撐著。

countries: 交戰方是英國與西班牙拉普拉塔河總督區。英方由皇家海軍與皇家陸軍組成的遠征體系主導：海軍分隊由海軍少將約翰·波帕姆指揮，十數艘戰列艦與巡洋艦封鎖河口，並抽調海軍陸戰隊、艦上水兵與隨艦炮兵組成可登陸作戰的步兵支隊；陸軍方面則從駐紮好望角與英屬西非據點的正規步兵團分遣隊，加上皇家炮兵，湊成約一千六百至一千八百人的登陸縱隊，第二年再由海軍准將查爾斯·科頓率大隊援軍抵達。英軍在好望角設有基地，遠征所需的糧秣、火藥、攻城器材與傷員後送全靠繞好望角的海上航線維持，戰役節奏因此被船期牢牢綁住。西班牙一方是拉普拉塔河總督區：總督索布雷蒙特侯爵在英軍逼近時棄城而去，權力一度落在布宜諾斯艾利斯市議會與克里奧爾民兵手中；城防主力是首都常備兵（邊防兵團與固定營）、克里奧爾城市民兵，以及從潘帕斯各省、上秘魯與庫尤方向趕來的志願兵，另有以長矛、火槍與騎兵為主的鄉村游擊武裝「蒙托內拉」。蒙得維的亞由王室總督府直接控制，是西班牙在河口唯一的海軍基地與後方樞紐，守軍由方哈維爾·德埃利奧指揮；它與布宜諾斯艾利斯之間在指揮權與貿易利益上早有裂痕，這道裂痕在戰事中被放大。
countriesEn: The belligerents were Britain and Spain's Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. On the British side the war was fought by a combined expedition of the Royal Navy and the Royal Army. The naval squadron was commanded by Rear Admiral John Popham: a dozen ships of the line and cruisers blockaded the mouth of the river, and detachments of Royal Marines, ship's sailors and naval gunners were formed into a brigade capable of fighting on shore. The army contribution was drawn from detachments of regular foot regiments stationed at the Cape and in West African garrisons, together with the Royal Artillery, adding up to a landing force of roughly sixteen hundred to eighteen hundred men; a year later a much larger reinforcement arrived under Commodore Charles Cotton. Britain kept a base at the Cape, and every round of biscuit, powder, siege material and wounded had to travel around the Cape by sea, so the rhythm of the campaign was dictated by sailing schedules. On the Spanish side stood the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. When the British closed in, the viceroy, the Marquis of Sobremonte, abandoned the city, and power passed for a time to the Cabildo of Buenos Aires and the criollo militia. The defence of the capital rested on the regular troops of the capital (the Frontier Battalion and the Fixeds), the criollo urban militia, and volunteer columns arriving from the Pampas provinces, from Upper Peru and from Cuyo, together with a rural irregular force, the montoneras, armed with lances, muskets and horses. Montevideo was under the direct authority of the royal government in Madrid; it was Spain's only naval base and logistical hub in the estuary, and its garrison was commanded by Francisco Javier de Elío. Relations between Montevideo and Buenos Aires were already bad, divided by questions of command and commercial interest, and the war widened that rift.
people: 波帕姆海軍少將促成了第一次遠征，但真正決定攻城節奏的是陸軍少將威廉·埃爾芬斯頓，他率領的支隊是全軍骨幹；1806年7月5日反擊失敗後，埃爾芬斯頓在撤退途中於馬爾克斯橋一帶陣亡，被鄉村騎兵的長矛刺中，隨軍的拉爾夫·埃爾韋斯准將在8月率一支縱隊企圖捲土重來，卻在聖安東尼奧被武裝村民與高卓騎兵殲滅，埃爾韋斯重傷被俘，第一次遠征就此瓦解。第二次遠征由陸軍中將約翰·惠特洛克全權指揮，海軍由科頓准將配合，攻略重心放在蒙得維的亞；英軍在布宜諾斯艾利斯以北屢遭聯邦騎兵與民兵擾亂，6月初的一場前哨戰迫其退回，最終是6月7日馬爾克斯橋之役打通通往城郊的道路，但隨即在僵持中收到歐洲的消息。西班牙一方的關鍵人物是卡塔隆尼亞出身的軍人聖地亞哥·德·利涅爾斯：他以邊疆騎兵指揮官的身分在1806年7月5日率民兵主動出擊反制英軍，8月12日率援軍接管首府，1807年被任命為總督；他在1807年拒絕與英軍在開闊地交鋒，把兵線退到城郊既定陣地，最終在援軍未至、糧彈告急之下簽署降書。曼努埃爾·貝爾格拉諾從上秘魯率「北方援軍」南下，穩住了民兵陣線並牽制了蒙得維的亞方向；胡安·馬丁·德普耶雷多與科爾內利奧·薩阿維德拉分別在邊境與河口上游集結兵力；方哈維爾·德埃利奧死守蒙得維的亞至最後；特魯科三兄弟率奎爾梅斯一帶的民兵在鄉間屢次襲擊英軍縱隊，說明地方武裝在整場戰役中的分量。
peopleEn: Rear Admiral John Popham set the first expedition in motion, but the officer who really set the pace of the assault on the city was Major General William Elphinstone, whose brigade was the backbone of the force. After the counter-attack of 5 July 1806 had turned into a retreat, Elphinstone was killed near the Puente de Márquez, run through by the lance of a country horseman. Brigadier General Ralph Elwes, who accompanied him, landed a column in August to retrieve the position and was annihilated at San Antonio by armed villagers and gaucho horse, Elwes himself being wounded and taken prisoner; with that the first invasion collapsed. The second expedition was commanded by Lieutenant General John Whitelocke, with Commodore Charles Cotton cooperating at sea; the plan of campaign centred on Montevideo. North of Buenos Aires the British were repeatedly worried by federal cavalry and militia, and a skirmish in early June 1807 drove them back before the bridge of the Puente de Márquez on 7 June opened the road to the outskirts; the advance then stalled in a stalemate that was broken by news from Europe. The decisive figure on the Spanish side was Santiago de Liniers, a Catalan career officer. As commander of the frontier horse he led the militia counter-attack that checked the British on 5 July 1806; on 12 August he took over the capital with the reinforcements, and in 1807 he was appointed viceroy. In 1807 he refused to meet the British in open ground, drew his line back to prepared positions outside the city, and finally signed the capitulation with reinforcements absent and ammunition running short. Manuel Belgrano marched south from Upper Peru with the northern auxiliary army, steadied the militia line and tied down the Montevideo side. Juan Martín de Pueyrredón and Cornelio Saavedra raised forces on the frontier and in the upper reaches of the estuary. Francisco Javier de Elío held Montevideo to the last. The three Truco brothers, leading the Quilmes country militia, harried British columns in the interior and showed how much of the campaign was actually decided by local armed groups.
kits: 卡面這件燧發槍是英國陸軍自1703年起定裝的「布朗·貝斯」式燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約十四點五毫米（0.577 英寸），配一顆約四十三公克的鉛彈，槍身用橡木與胡桃木，機件為鑄鐵，擊錘打擊燧石取火。它在十八世紀末至十九世紀初的英軍步槍團中是標準裝備，遠征拉普拉塔河的兩支英軍縱隊所用的正是這一型。燧發機關免去火繩的引火藥與明火，比火繩槍更適合南半球多風的草原，射擊時也不必暴露火光與硝煙。射程方面，有效射擊距離約在一百至二百公尺，超出此距彈丸跳飛，線性橫排的密集齊射在兩三百公尺內最為有效。射速方面，受過裝填與立射訓練的步兵每分鐘可發三至四發，但整齊齊射要求全排同步，實際上每分鐘一至兩發方能維持陣形。裝備體系上，英軍步兵以燧發滑膛槍配刺刀，騎兵用一七九六年式卡賓槍與一七九六年式手槍，炮兵配六磅與九磅野戰砲，遠征軍另攜二十四磅臼砲與攻城器材。防守方的西班牙殖民軍同樣大量裝備英製燧發步槍——西班牙王室早於十八世紀就向英國訂購「布朗·貝斯」，稱之為「溫莎步槍」，這些槍與本地土造火槍、獵槍並存，是市區民兵手中最常見的火器；守軍另有四磅至十二磅的銅砲與臼砲，城市與外圍砲壘共佈置數十門炮，步兵再配長矛與獵刀，鄉村騎兵則以長矛衝鋒。運輸方面，英軍一切靠船，攻城所需火藥、木料在河口沒有來源，須由艦隊海路運來，陸戰隊還要靠灘頭小艇與平底船在淺水處轉運。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the flintlock smoothbore musket that Britain's army standardised from 1703, the 'Brown Bess': a calibre of about 14.5 millimetres (0.577 inch), firing a lead ball of roughly forty-three grams, a stock of oak and walnut, and a lock of cast iron in which the hammer strikes a flint to make the spark. It was standard equipment in British foot regiments from the late eighteenth into the early nineteenth century, and the two British columns sent against the Río de la Plata were armed with exactly this pattern. A flint mechanism needs neither priming powder nor an open flame, so it is far better suited to the windy grasslands of the southern hemisphere and it no longer betrays the shooter's position with a glowing match and drifting smoke. As for range, effective musket fire ran to something like one hundred to two hundred metres; beyond that the ball jumps, and it is the dense linear volley at two or three hundred metres that does the damage. As for rate of fire, a trained infantryman could get off three or four rounds a minute, but a true simultaneous volley required the whole rank to fire together, so in practice the line could only sustain one or two rounds a minute and still keep its order. Across the British system, infantry carried flintlock muskets with bayonets, cavalry used the 1796 pattern carbine and the 1796 pattern pistol, the artillery brought six- and nine-pounder field guns, and the expedition added twenty-four-pounder howitzers and siege material. The colonial Spanish forces were also heavily equipped with British flintlock muskets: the Spanish crown had been buying Brown Bess guns in England since the eighteenth century, calling them the 'Windsor musket', and these stood side by side with locally made matchlocks and hunting guns as the commonest arm in the hands of the city militia. The defenders also had bronze guns and howitzers from four to twelve pounds, with several dozen pieces distributed among the city batteries and the outer works; infantry were armed with lances and hunting knives, and the country horse fought with the lance. On the logistics side, everything the British needed came by sea: powder and timber could not be produced in the estuary and had to be carried round by the squadron, while the landing parties used boats and flat-bottomed craft to shift men and stores across the shallows.
tactics: 第一次遠征，英軍的戰法由海軍先手：艦隊封鎖河口，用艦炮與灘頭炮兵壓制外圍工事，登陸部隊以縱隊沿海岸公路推進，攻市時採兩翼分進、逐次攻擊外圍據點，再以縱隊插入缺口直取市中心。7月5日的反擊與隨後的撤退暴露了兩個弱點：糧秣車隊與攻城器材沿單一道路行進，撤退時成為首當其衝的獵物；步兵縱隊一旦被鄉村騎兵繞到側後，就難以維持縱隊秩序。第二次遠征，英軍改為先取蒙得維的亞，1807年1月封鎖港口、2月5日夜襲城區與城堡，再沿海岸公路北上，以師級縱隊交替掩護推進。英軍在聖伊西德羅一線屢遭聯邦騎兵與民兵的側擊，屢次停頓，重新集結後才奪取馬爾克斯橋，占領「四豌豆」莊園與中途驛站，逼近城郊後卻四面作戰、糧秣線拉長。西班牙方則以守城為主：利用壕溝與外圍土壘遲滯英軍，集中兵力於夜間或清晨突然出擊，以市區建築與廢墟作掩體，並不斷以蒙托內拉騎兵襲擊英軍的糧秣線與偵察隊。1807年6月，英軍在開闊地帶逼近時，守軍主動收縮陣線，把決戰地點移到城郊的既定陣地，最後在援軍未至、彈藥告急的情況下接受投降。
tacticsEn: In the first invasion the British method began with the navy. The squadron blockaded the estuary, used ship guns and beach artillery to batter the outer works, and marched the landing force inland in column along the coast road. The assault on the city was made by two wings moving separately, taking the outlying positions one after another, and then driving columns through the gaps towards the centre. The counter-attack of 5 July and the retreat that followed exposed two weaknesses: the baggage train and the siege material moved along a single road and became the first prey of the retreat, and an infantry column once flanked by country horse could no longer keep its order. The second expedition changed method: take Montevideo first, blockade the port in January 1807, storm the town and the citadel on the night of 5 February, then march north along the coast road with divisions covering one another in turn. The British were checked repeatedly by federal horse and militia around San Isidro, had to halt and reform, and only then took the Puente de Márquez, the 'Four Peas' ranch and the posting station on the road, arriving before the outskirts of the city with their communications stretched on every side. The Spanish method was essentially defensive: hold the line with ditches and earthworks outside the walls, mass the troops for sudden attacks by night or at daybreak, use the buildings and ruins of the city as cover, and send the montoneras time and again against British baggage lines and scouting parties. In June 1807, when the British advanced across open ground, the defenders deliberately contracted their line and fixed the decisive battle on the prepared positions outside the city, and accepted surrender only when reinforcements had not come and ammunition was running out.
data: 可核的數字有限，以下為各來源常見的量級，說法互有出入。第一次遠征的船隊約十八艘戰列艦，登陸作戰的兵力約一千六百至一千八百人，加上艦上水手與炮組，攻城總兵力在三千五百至四千人之間；英軍在7月5日攻市中陣亡約二百餘人，其中就包括陣亡的埃爾芬斯頓，負傷者約七百上下，俘虜與失散者數百；西班牙與民兵方面的損失估計在數百至一千餘之間。8月26日聖安東尼奧之戰，埃爾韋斯的縱隊約一千二百人，除死傷外被俘六百上下，二十四門炮盡失，入侵軍於9月初完全退出。第二次遠征兵力約一萬至一萬二千人，艦隊戰列艦十八至二十艘；1807年1月至2月的蒙得維的亞之戰，英軍損失約一千人，攻城中傷亡最重；6月初的前哨戰英軍死傷數百，6月7日馬爾克斯橋之戰後英軍死傷與被俘合計逾兩千人。守軍在布宜諾斯艾利斯的常備與民兵合計約三千五百至四千人，另有數千鄉村武裝。就航程而言，從英國繞好望角到拉普拉塔河口的單程約一萬海里，一支遠征分隊往返一次耗時以月計，遠征成本因此遠高於歐洲戰場。
dataEn: The record is thin and the figures below are the orders of magnitude most sources give, with wide disagreement between them. The first expedition's squadron numbered about eighteen ships of the line; the landing force was some sixteen hundred to eighteen hundred men, and with the sailors and gun crews aboard ship the total strength present at the assault lay between three thousand five hundred and four thousand. In the attack of 5 July the British lost around two hundred men killed, Elphinstone among them, roughly seven hundred wounded, and several hundred taken or scattered; Spanish and militia losses are estimated anywhere from several hundred to more than a thousand. At the battle of San Antonio on 26 August, Elwes's column of about twelve hundred men lost some six hundred prisoners besides its dead and wounded, and all twenty-four of its guns; the invading force was completely out of the river by early September. The second expedition brought between ten thousand and twelve thousand men and eighteen to twenty ships of the line. The fighting at Montevideo between January and February 1807 cost the British roughly a thousand men, the heaviest losses falling in the assault on the city; the skirmish in early June cost them several hundred, and after the bridge of the Puente de Márquez on 7 June their killed, wounded and captured together exceeded two thousand. The Spanish garrison and militia in Buenos Aires together numbered about three thousand five hundred to four thousand, with several thousand more in the country bands. As for distance: the run from Britain round the Cape to the mouth of the Río de la Plata was of the order of ten thousand miles, and a single round trip by a detached squadron took months, which made the expedition far more expensive than any campaign in Europe.
cause: 遠征的起因並非領土爭端，而是帝國貿易與海上權力。1804年英西結盟對付拿破崙，卻同時維持著一份西班牙殖民貿易的壟斷安排：南美物產必須經指定的西班牙港口與官方商行輸出，英國商人只能以夾板船和走私的方式經營。1780年代起英國在拉普拉塔河的走私船隊與貨物數量急增，與西班牙當局的摩擦層出不窮；1806年4月至5月蒙得維的亞爆發騷動，克里奧爾商人與經手英國貨物的西班牙商人發生衝突，波及英籍商人與英國船隻，英國海軍隨即出面交涉。與此同時，拿破崙戰爭使英國需要把海上封鎖線延伸到南美，切斷法國與其西班牙美洲盟友的貿易，並保護運往英國的銀礦物資與白銀船隊。波帕姆奉命率分隊南下，表面上護航與交涉，實際帶有以海軍壓力迫使總督府開放口岸、承認英國貿易地位的意圖。英方低估了布宜諾斯艾利斯民兵與鄉村武裝的抵抗能力，也低估了河口潮汐、淺灘、缺糧與超長補給線，會讓每一次登陸與推進都付出額外代價。
causeEn: The expedition was not about territory. It was about imperial trade and command of the sea. Britain and Spain had allied against Napoleon in 1804, yet the arrangement rested on a Spanish monopoly over colonial trade: produce from South America had to pass through designated Spanish ports and the official merchant houses, and British traders could only work the trade with clippers and smuggling. From the 1780s the number of British smuggler vessels and the volume of their cargoes in the Río de la Plata grew fast, and friction with the Spanish authorities was constant. In April and May 1806 riots broke out in Montevideo between criollo merchants and Spanish traders handling British goods, dragging British merchants and British shipping into the disturbance, and the Royal Navy came forward to argue the point. Meanwhile the Napoleonic War pushed Britain to extend its blockade to South America, to cut France off from its Spanish-American allies and to protect the bullion and silver fleets running to Britain. Popham's squadron sailed south under orders that covered escort duty and negotiation but carried, in substance, the intention of using sea power to force the viceroy to open the ports and recognise British trading rights. The British underestimated the resistance of the Buenos Aires militia and the country bands, and they underestimated the tide, the shoals, the shortage of food and the enormous length of the supply line, each of which made every landing and every advance cost more than it should.
impact: 這場遠征在軍事上以失敗告終，卻留下幾項長遠影響。其一，它證明以正面強攻拿下設防良好的殖民地首府，代價遠高於歐洲戰場；1806年7月的失利與1807年2月蒙得維的亞的傷亡，之後被寫進英國陸軍的戰術教材，成為反對盲攻的證據。其二，1808年英軍把遠征重心轉向太平洋岸的秘魯與智利時，決策者引用的正是拉普拉塔河的教訓；同一支艦隊與一批久經遠征的官兵，隨即出現在卡亞俄與海濱的戰役裡。其三，遠征沒有奪取殖民地，卻改變了布宜諾斯艾利斯的城市面貌：兩次圍城之後，首都加固了城牆與外圍砲壘，炮兵名冊與守備編制重新編訂，「民兵守城」從此成為這座城市的政治記憶，並在1809年至1810年間被反覆引用於自治與革命的論述之中。其四，英國遠征軍在1807年因歐洲局勢逆轉而撤退，隨行的部分老兵被編入新成立的步兵營，成為日後與遠征相關的正規化部隊；而馬德里的波旁王朝在拿破崙壓力下崩解之後，英西兩國由盟友變成交戰者，拉普拉塔河的攻守關係在幾個月內完全倒轉過來。
impactEn: The expedition failed militarily, but it left several consequences behind. First, it demonstrated that storming a well-defended colonial capital by direct assault cost far more than anything in Europe; the reverse of 5 July 1806 and the slaughter of the assault on Montevideo in February 1807 were later written into British army tactical literature as evidence against blind attacks. Second, when in 1808 Britain swung the weight of its expedition to the Pacific shores of Peru and Chile, the decision-makers quoted the Río de la Plata lesson; the same squadrons and the same long-service soldiers appeared shortly afterwards at Callao and along the coast. Third, the expedition took no colony, but it changed the face of Buenos Aires: after the two sieges the capital reinforced its walls and outer batteries, the artillery establishment and the garrison were reorganized, and 'the city defended by its own militia' became part of the city's political memory, invoked repeatedly in the arguments over autonomy and revolution between 1809 and 1810. Fourth, the British withdrew in 1807 as the situation in Europe turned against the war, and some of the older soldiers who had served in South America were formed into newly raised battalions that became the standing units later associated with the expedition. And once the Bourbon monarchy in Madrid collapsed under Napoleon's pressure, Britain and Spain changed from allies into enemies, so the whole relationship of attack and defence in the Río de la Plata was inverted within a few months.
result: 結果是兩次遠征都沒有把殖民地變成英國的屬地。第一次遠征在1806年7月的反擊與8月聖安東尼奧的殲滅戰之後解體，英軍於9月初撤出河口。第二次遠征以1807年1月攻下蒙得維的亞、6月14日迫使布宜諾斯艾利斯簽署降書告一段落，但降約條件是英軍不得攻掠市區、須按禮移交守軍，實際上是一場有條件的停火。1807年6月底起，歐洲的消息——巴約訥的退位與法軍進入西班牙——傳到河口，英國政府更替後決定停止攻勢，英軍於7月撤出布宜諾斯艾利斯，8月把蒙得維的亞交還西班牙守軍，遠征軍陸續返航。最終的戰果是一場不划算的勝利代價：英國出動了遠征兵力的大部分，卻只換來數月的實際控制，沒有一寸永久收益，戰事中真正得利者是重新掌握主動權的西班牙總督府與布宜諾斯艾利斯的克里奧爾民兵。遠洋封鎖與遠征在技術上可行，在政治上卻難以長期維持，這場拉普拉塔河的攻防於是成了十八世紀末大西洋世界的一個轉折點。
resultEn: Neither expedition turned the colony into a British possession. The first collapsed after the counter-attack of 5 July 1806 and the destruction of Elwes's column at San Antonio in August; the British were out of the river by early September. The second ended in a stage of success: the taking of Montevideo in January 1807, and the capitulation of Buenos Aires on 14 June 1807. But the terms were those of an armistice rather than a conquest — the British were to leave the city undamaged and the garrison was to be allowed to depart with honours. From late June 1807 the news from Europe, the abdications at Bayonne and the French entry into Spain, reached the estuary; a new British ministry decided to stop the offensive, the army left Buenos Aires in July, Montevideo was handed back to the Spanish garrison in August, and the expedition sailed home in stages. The result was a victory bought at a price that made it a loss: Britain had committed the greater part of its expeditionary force and gained a few months of effective control and not a mile of permanent territory, while the real gain of the war fell to the Spanish viceroyalty, which regained the initiative, and to the criollo militia of Buenos Aires, which had proved it could fight. Ocean blockade and amphibious expedition were technically feasible but politically impossible to sustain, and the struggle in the Río de la Plata therefore stands as a turning point in the Atlantic world of the late eighteenth century.
